question: In congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO), Crigler massage is performed by applying firm downward pressure over the lacrimal sac to hydrostically rupture the membranous obstruction at the valve of Hasner.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The Crigler massage technique applies firm downward pressure over the lacrimal sac (between the medial canthus and nasal bone), creating hydrostatic pressure in the duct to rupture the membranous valve of Hasner at the distal end of the nasolacrimal duct — the commonest site of obstruction in CNLDO.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Crigler (hydrostatic) massage applies firm downward pressure from the medial canthus towards the nasal alae, compressing the lacrimal sac and directing hydraulic force through the nasolacrimal duct to rupture the imperforate membrane at the valve of Hasner. It is first-line management from birth to 12 months and achieves spontaneous resolution in approximately 90% of cases by 12 months.
